transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-12
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Alex Soto (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM); Jordan Lee (CISO), Sara Patel (Head of Infra), Miguel Torres (DevSecOps), Anika Rao (Legal/SecOps)
Recorded via Fireflies

Summary:
High-level readout of recent external penetration test (red team) and internal vulnerability scan; align on remediation priorities, patching cadence, and SDLC gating changes to prevent regressions. Discussed audit log retention and KMS encryption model for private deployments. Agreed on action items and a follow-up hands-on validation session.

Topics:
- Pen-test findings (3 high, 7 medium, 12 low)
- Immediate mitigations vs long-term fixes
- Patch cadence and emergency response windows
- Secure SDLC gating (SCA, IaC scanning, pre-prod gating)
- RBAC/SSO implications and audit log collection for compliance
- Encryption/KMS model for private VPC deployment

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll do a quick roll call and then Alex will run through the pen test highlights. Jordan, Sara, Miguel — thanks for making time.
[00:22] Jordan Lee: yep thanks, on my side, we got the report last week and we've triaged a bunch, but we want to make sure the mitigations map back to our SLA and compliance controls.
[00:35] Alex Soto: Cool, I'll start with the high-level. The external red team surfaced three high-risk issues. Two are misconfigurations around our older ingress rule sets — basically overly permissive ALB listeners in a staging environment that had credentials cached in logs. The third was an exposed admin console with weak session timeout.
[01:05] Sara Patel: sorry, can you clarify "credentials cached in logs" — are we talking application logs or a misconfigured exporter?
[01:12] Alex Soto: It looks like app logs where a debug flag was left on in a staging replicate; some bearer tokens were slipped into structured logs. Not production keys but still sensitive. The finding references CVE style notes but it's more of a config issue.
[01:28] Miguel Torres: yeah that matches what we saw — staging had a longer retention for debug logs while we triaged a separate incident last month. We've since toggled the flags but need to sanitize historical logs.
[01:40] Priya Nair: quick Q — does Redwood have a recommended retention policy or a tool to help with log redaction in private deployments?
[01:48] Alex Soto: We recommend 90 days for structured request logs and 365 days for audit-only entries in enterprise. For redaction, we can push a sidecar or parser that strips known patterns; we also integrate with customer KMS to re-encrypt sensitive fragments. We'll link the doc.
[02:10] Jordan Lee: second high was the admin console. What was severity and recommended mitigation?
[02:16] Alex Soto: Admin console had an auth bypass in an older UI route when SSO was misrouted — root cause was an old session cookie not expiring. Short-term we suggested disabling legacy auth endpoints and enforcing SAML on that route. Long-term, rotate session handling and add a platform-level WAF rule.
[02:40] Miguel Torres: can we get patch details? Is this something we need to schedule an immediate hotfix for?
[02:46] Alex Soto: The vendor already has a patch in v1.8.4 — so yes, plan a hotfix for the admin nodes in staging then promote to canary. We'll help validate.
[03:00] Jordan Lee: third high?
[03:02] Alex Soto: third is a privilege escalation chain during container breakout tests — they showed a path via a deprecated SSH service left on an admin bastion image. Not an issue in prod images, but it was enough for red team to demonstrate lateral movement in the test env.
[03:20] Sara Patel: ugh that's on our build pipeline; we had an old AMI baking in legacy daemons. We'll need to scrub builders.
[03:27] Maya Chen: sounds like secure SDLC changes — shift-left IaC and image hardening. Alex, do you have recommended tools?
[03:34] Alex Soto: For IaC scanning we usually recommend pre-commit hooks plus SCA in pipeline — e.g., GitHub Advanced Security or Snyk for code and IaC. For images, we suggest SBOM generation and image signing; we can supply a reference pipeline that includes Trivy and in-pipeline gating.
[03:55] Miguel Torres: On SBOMs, how does Redwood expect customers to share them for private deployments? We have concerns about data residency.
[04:02] Alex Soto: SBOMs can be stored in customer-managed S3 in their region; Redwood will reference but not ingest the raw SBOM unless you opt into hosted analysis. For Private mode the control plane pointers are all customer-hosted and metadata stays within your VPC.
[04:20] Jordan Lee: good. Let's talk about audit logs and SOC 2 expectations — retention, immutability, and proof for auditors.
[04:27] Maya Chen: Jordan, we have a SOC 2 package and audit logs schema. Redwood can export signed audit bundles to your KMS-backed bucket. You can define retention and legal holds for the auditor timeframe.
[04:40] Anika Rao: For auditors we need chain of custody and key rotation evidence — do you support HSM-backed keys or BYOK?
[04:48] Alex Soto: Yes, we integrate with customer KMS/HSM via external key management; BYOK is supported and rotation can be audited. We'll send the integration guide.
[05:00] Sara Patel: tagging back to patch cadence: we run monthly patch windows but sometimes urgent CVEs require off-cycle. The red team flagged CVE-2025-1122 as medium (container escape vector) — is that something Redwood can help validate post-patch?
[05:18] Alex Soto: Absolutely. We'll run an exploit validation on your staging once the hotfix is applied. Note: the pen-test report included CVE-2024-27219 as an example chain exploited via an outdated dependency in a third-party lib — we recommend dependency scanning and pinning.
[05:40] Miguel Torres: dependency pinning... we have Dependabot but it creates a lot of noise. How do you recommend triage?
[05:48] Alex Soto: Prioritize by exploitability and presence in production images. Use SBOM cross-referenced with runtime process map. Redwood's Optimize team can help prioritize to minimize noise — we can do a joint runbook.
[06:05] Jordan Lee: Any blockers on encryption? The report called out some ephemeral tokens logged in plaintext for a short time.
[06:12] Alex Soto: Short-term mitigation: rotate credentials and enforce full TLS for internal endpoints, plus suppress debug dumps. Long-term: adopt envelope encryption for all secrets at rest using your KMS and redact sensitive fields before writing to logs.
[06:30] Sara Patel: On RBAC and SSO — we want strict least privilege and SAML SSO; what are Redwood's capabilities for fine-grained role mapping?
[06:39] Maya Chen: Redwood supports SAML and OIDC, SCIM provisioning, and attribute-based role mapping. For private deployments you can bring your IdP; remote users are authenticated but roles are enforced locally with audit trails.
[06:55] Anika Rao: during audits, we need per-token audit lines and identity traces — does Redwood store token-level metadata?
[07:02] Alex Soto: We log token issuance events and can include token IDs in audit records. For high compliance customers we recommend forwarding audit logs to your SIEM via Kinesis/Forwarder; we can also provide signed bundles for auditors.
[07:20] Miguel Torres: about the historical logs we mentioned — is there a supported way to redact or remove specific artifacts from S3? We might need to produce a clean dataset for the folks doing the forensics.
[07:30] Alex Soto: You can do object-level rewriting to remove fields; Redwood has a redaction utility for structured logs we can run as a one-off. We'll need consent and the exact search strings.
[07:45] Jordan Lee: ok, shifting gears: patch cadence governance — we currently have monthly regular windows and emergency windows. The red team recommended moving some critical CVEs to a 48-hour SLA for patch verification. Is that realistic operationally?
[07:58] Sara Patel: 48 hours is tight for us but for high-severity CVEs we can do emergency hotfixes if we have clear owners and rollback plans.
[08:08] Maya Chen: Redwood's Dedicated customers often adopt a tiered SLA; we can mirror that — e.g., P1 in 48–72 hours with canary and rollback policies automated. We can recommend a runbook.
[08:22] Miguel Torres: automated rollback — do you have examples?
[08:25] Alex Soto: Yes, blue/green or canary promotions with automatic metric checks. If error budget or latency spikes exceed thresholds, we rollback and notify. We'll share a canonical k8s manifest and pipeline snippet.
[08:40] Jordan Lee: legal question — if we push a hotfix to private deployment, what level of change control is needed to keep us audit-ready?
[08:48] Anika Rao: We typically require a change record, review evidence, test results, and rollback plan — all timestamped and bundled.
[08:56] Maya Chen: Redwood can generate a change snapshot including SHA for image, CI run ID, test results, and an attestation. That helps for auditor chain-of-custody.
[09:08] Sara Patel: great. any recommendations about vulnerability triage meetings cadence?
[09:14] Alex Soto: We recommend weekly triage during the immediate remediation phase, then move to monthly once backlogged items are within SLA. Make sure to include product & legal for high-impact items.
[09:28] Jordan Lee: The pen test report called out 7 medium findings — can we briefly run through highest of those?
[09:35] Alex Soto: Sure — medium 1 is an S3 bucket ACL that allowed list access from non-prod accounts; medium 2 is outdated agent on some build nodes flagged by the internal scanner; medium 3 is an IaC misconfig that allowed broad network egress.
[09:55] Miguel Torres: the S3 ACLs were from a cross-account analytics job; we'll tighten the policy and reissue creds.
[10:02] Sara Patel: about build agents — how do you suggest we enforce agent updates? We have a fleet of build runners.
[10:09] Alex Soto: Use immutable runners with scheduled replacement and auto-terminate older runners; enforce image signing and SBOM checks. For an immediate step, schedule a forced rotation and update the AMI template.
[10:22] Priya Nair: Maya, do we have any redwood security contacts for SOC 2 evidence?
[10:27] Maya Chen: yes, I'll add our security & compliance mailbox and the auditor pack link in the follow-up.
[10:32] Jordan Lee: quick note on data residency — we store patient-adjacent data; any recommendations for regional restrictions?
[10:39] Alex Soto: For regulated datasets, run Redwood Private in your VPC in the region where data resides; control plane pointers can remain in region and all backups and logs stored in your account. We'll attach the private deployment topology diagram.
[10:55] Sara Patel: can Redwood support an air-gapped option if needed down the line?
[10:59] Alex Soto: Yes, we have an on-prem air-gapped package for enterprise; it's heavier op cost but supported. We'll include the checklist.
[11:08] Jordan Lee: any surprises in the pen test that we should be aware of?
[11:12] Alex Soto: The red team exploited a chain combining a misconfigured ingress, a debug flag, and an outdated third-party lib — it's the classic 'small issues combined' problem. No zero-day native Redwood runtime issues, which is good news.
[11:26] Maya Chen: that's encouraging. Let's talk timelines: Miguel, you mentioned toggling flags and rotating logs — can you estimate when you'll have staging sanitized?
[11:35] Miguel Torres: we should have staging cleaned and initial rotations done by 2025-08-14, assuming no blockers. We might need help on log redaction tooling.
[11:44] Alex Soto: Redwood SE team can run the redaction job; we'll need the search strings and S3 location.
[11:50] Jordan Lee: and for the admin console patch — Sara you said you can schedule a hotfix?
[11:54] Sara Patel: yes, propose to do hotfix on 2025-08-16 in the early window with rollback capability.
[12:01] Maya Chen: perfect. We'll also plan the follow-up validation session the week after — Alex and team to validate exploit chain and confirm regression tests.
[12:08] Miguel Torres: one last thing — can we get a sample SOC 2 control mapping for how these vulnerabilities map to CC6.1/CC7?
[12:17] Anika Rao: yes, auditors will want to see mapping to controls for remediation evidence.
[12:21] Maya Chen: we'll include a mapping doc showing pen-test findings -> remediation -> SOC 2 control references.
[12:29] Jordan Lee: ok, let's do a quick recap and owners.
[12:33] Maya Chen: recap: Redwood sends redacted pen-test + mitigation spreadsheet (Maya), Alex validates CVE/exploit on staging (Alex), Helix provides staging kubeconfig & inventory (Miguel), hotfix scheduled for admin nodes (Sara), follow-up validation week of 2025-08-19.
[12:52] Miguel Torres: noted. Thanks everyone.
[12:55] Maya Chen: thanks, we'll follow up with the links and schedule invites.
[13:00] Meeting end.

References/Artifacts mentioned:
